summary.text: An Egyptian Desert Father also called John the Short. His received stories emphasize humility, work, obedience, and the guidance of other monks.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: The OCA places John’s desert ascetic life in fifth-century Egypt and relates that he entered monastic life with his brother. His epithet distinguishes this John from other saints of the same name.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: One story contrasts his wish to live without bodily necessities with his return hungry to the community. Another describes the long watering of dry wood that finally bears fruit. These are transmitted monastic teaching narratives, not a new prayer rule for readers.

blocks.text: John became a spiritual guide. The OCA’s life of Saint Arsenius the Great recounts how John received the former courtier, tested his humility, and accepted him into monastic life.
